identity.title: Panic/anxiety features: episodes at rest or with stress, dread, paresthesias, known panic disorder; not affected by sleep

technique.how: Ask whether the patient carries a diagnosis of panic disorder, whether episodes occur at rest or with emotional stress, are accompanied by dread, paresthesias or hyperventilation, whether they are affected by sleep (wake the patient / occur during sleep), and whether they occur at work. Record episode duration.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to give a history; ideally corroborate with a witness or prior records.

interpretation.positive_finding: A known history of panic disorder makes a clinically significant arrhythmia somewhat less likely (LR 0.26, CI crosses 1). Panic features do not exclude arrhythmia; SVT is frequently misdiagnosed as panic.
interpretation.negative_finding: Palpitations that are affected by sleeping (LR 2.29) or occur at work (LR 2.17) modestly favour a cardiac arrhythmia over anxiety.
interpretation.pitfalls: Anxiety and arrhythmia coexist; paroxysmal SVT commonly produces panic-like symptoms and is mislabelled as panic disorder. History alone cannot exclude arrhythmia, so symptom-rhythm correlation is still required.
interpretation.changes_what: Panic features lower but do not remove arrhythmia probability; still obtain ECG and, if recurrent, ambulatory monitoring for symptom-rhythm correlation.

estimates.target_condition: Clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia (finding: known history of panic disorder)
estimates.population: Adults presenting with palpitations (RCE pooled 7 accuracy studies; this feature from single-study data)
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmia after ambulatory ECG monitoring / clinical work-up
estimates.quote: A known history of panic disorder (LR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.07-1.01) or having palpitations lasting less than 5 minutes (LR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.22-0.63)

estimates.target_condition: Clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia (finding: palpitations affected by sleeping - the converse of this record's 'not affected by sleep')
estimates.population: Adults presenting with palpitations (single-study data within RCE)
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmia after ambulatory ECG monitoring / clinical work-up
estimates.quote: having palpitations affected by sleeping (LR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.33-3.94), or while the patient is at work (LR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.19-3.96)

estimates.target_condition: Clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia (finding: palpitations occurring while at work)
estimates.population: Adults presenting with palpitations (single-study data within RCE)
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis of cardiac arrhythmia after ambulatory ECG monitoring / clinical work-up
estimates.quote: having palpitations affected by sleeping (LR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.33-3.94), or while the patient is at work (LR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.19-3.96)

sources.citation: Thavendiranathan P, Bagai A, Khoo C, Dorian P, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with palpitations have a cardiac arrhythmia? JAMA. 2009;302(19):2135-2143.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use panic features to dismiss palpitations with syncope, exertional onset, structural heart disease, or an abnormal ECG.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Palpitations with syncope, chest pain, or haemodynamic compromise need ECG and monitoring regardless of anxiety history.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data for panic-feature history reported in the RCE (per abstract).

extraction_notes: Only the JAMA abstract was accessible (not in PMC); locations are 'Abstract, Results'. The RCE states 'Most data were obtained from single studies with small sample sizes' so evidence_level is set to single_study. Only LRs for feature-present are reported; no LR for absence, no sens/spec pair -> partially_quantified. The panic-disorder LR 0.26 has CI 0.07-1.01 (crosses 1). 'Affected by sleeping' and 'at work' are entered as their own findings (LR when present); this record's 'not affected by sleep' is their absence, for which no LR was reported. The abstract also reports palpitations lasting <5 minutes LR 0.38 (0.22-0.63) (Abstract, Results); not entered because it is a separate finding.
